This tier is for region P2 and nothing else: every proposal must be a node of P2, and the captain lands it under that region. A proposal outside P2 will not be landed, however true or cheap it is.

Write your proposal to `c:/Users/dibuj/dev/rule30/blueprint/proposals/next.json` as one JSON document of this exact shape:

```json
{"proposals": [
  {"id": "<node id>", "lean_name": "<theorem name>",
   "statement": "theorem <theorem name> ... := by\n  sorry",
   "reason": "<why it is true, in English>",
   "disclaims": "<what it does NOT prove; empty for most nodes>",
   "route": {"tactics": "<tactic block>", "imports": []},
   "witness": {"expression": "<Bool-valued Lean expression>", "imports": [], "range": "<the finite range it covers>"}}

```

`id`, `lean_name`, `statement` and `reason` are required; `disclaims`, `route` and `witness` are optional and a missing one claims nothing. The harness checks every route and witness after this session ends, and a captain reads the check before the proposal.

End every turn with the structured report. Set `outcome` to `proposed` only once the file is written and you are done, `in_progress` while you are still working, and `abandoned` if you give up; fill in `journal` at the end.

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TzrZ59KG6aEPxNBEYGUoHj","type":"tool_result","content":"1	# Prize 2's residual: any bound on the centre column's excess that uses rule 30
2	
3	Talus, theorist, 2026-09-10.
4	
5	**The band first, because the project's rule says so.** **Project-internal.**
6	The topic asked for a negative if that is the honest answer, and it is: no bound
7	on the centre column's excess is reachable without a genuinely new idea, and
8	the reason is a fence (`C2`) rather than a measurement. Everything measured
9	here — the excess to `10^7` rows, its sign changes, its extremes, the
10	run-length distribution, the excess at every sparse set rule 30 supplies, and
11	the forcing laws' coverage — is **inside a fair coin's own scatter**, and the
12	three statistics that looked otherwise failed a 40-draw null. One small **known**
13	result is re-derived (Wolfram 1986 §7) with a consequence not in print (`C1`),
14	and one elementary row identity and row bound are new-but-small (`C3`, `C4`),
15	neither about the centre column. Nothing here touches Prize 2.
16	
17	## 1. The residual, in one paragraph
18	
19	Time runs down the picture; the centre column is the vertical read at `x = 0`,
20	one cell per row. Prize 2 says the black cells of that column are half of it in
21	the limit, and the board has already turned that into a statement with no
22	division in it: with `count(N)` the black cells among the first `N`, the excess
23	`E(N) = 2·count(N) − N` must be `o(N)`
24	(`centerColumn_density_tendsto_half_iff_excess`). What is missing is not a
25	better reformulation. It is **one true sentence about `E(N)` that is false for
26	some Bool sequence** — anything that uses the automaton at all. Twelve P2 nodes
27	are proved and ten are counting identities that hold of any `ℕ → Bool`; the two
28	that name rule 30 name it trivially. So the residual is not "prove
29	`E(N) = o(N)`" so much as "say *anything* about `E(N)` that a coin could fail",
30	and the reason that is hard can be put in one line: **rule 30 is a law along a
31	row, and the centre column is transverse to every row.** The rule constrains
32	three horizontally adjacent cells; two adjacent black cells in a row forbid a
33	cell of the next row, and that is a real constraint with real consequences
34	(§3, `C3`, `C4`). Two vertically adjacent cells of the centre column forbid
35	nothing, and cannot, because by crystal 40 the centre column is a **free
36	coordinate**: for every Bool sequence `b` there is a configuration, white at
37	every `x ≥ 1` at time `0`, whose centre column is exactly `b`. The residual
38	therefore lives in the one place that is not free — the left cone, the leftmost
39	black cell, the same ingredient Jen's and Kopra's theorems need for P1 — and
40	the only thing the cone gives the centre column is a bound on its **runs**,
41	which is capped in principle at `|E(N)| ≤ N(1 − 1/(c·log N))` and cannot reach
42	`o(N)` however sharp it is made.
43	
44	## 2. Why the known routes fail
45	
46	**On the board already.**
47	
48	- *"The centre column as a boundary condition"* (obstruction 2) and *"An
49	  eventually periodic centre column does not force another periodic column"*
50	  (obstruction 9, mine) end at the same place: a statement proved for an
51	  arbitrary `Config` is a statement about every `X_b`, and every Bool sequence
52	  is some `X_b`'s centre column. Written for P1; it applies verbatim to P2, and
53	  it is what kills route (2) below.
54	- *"Unbounded right-diagonal periods do not force an aperiodic centre column"*
55	  (obstruction 20, mine, this morning) closes the right edge for P1 and says
56	  the same thing from the other side: the centre column is the free bit of the
57	  right-diagonal tower, so no statistic of the tower separates the seed from a
58	  periodic boundary. Its closing line asked for a third death of that shape
59	  before an obstruction entry could say the family is statistically
60	  indistinguishable. §3's `C2` and the coverage table below are that third
61	  death, and the entry is appended to `docs/obstructions.md`.
62	- **Crystal 66, the OR-to-XOR filter — run, not asserted**
63	  (`explorer/talus7_filter.mjs`, single seed, 2,000 rows, rules 30, 150, 90,
64	  86, 110, 60). It changed one of my claims and strengthened another:
65	
66	  | rule | black runs in the centre column | alternation (`C1`) fails | `b(t+1)+2b(t) ≤ 4t+5` (`C3`) fails | triangle density |
67	  |---|---|---|---|---|
68	  | **30** | 474 (longest 9) | **0 / 968** | 0 / 1998, tight | 0.5008 |
69	  | 150 | none — the column is constantly black | vacuous | 0 / 1998, tight | 0.1090 |
70	  | 90 | none | vacuous | 0 / 1998 | 0.0391 |
71	  | **86** (rule 30 mirrored) | 474 (longest 9) | **316 / 968** | 0 / 1998, tight | 0.5008 |
72	  | 110 | none | vacuous | 0 / 1998 | 0.2942 |
73	  | 60 | none | vacuous | 0 / 1998 | 0.0391 |
74	
75	  `C1` **passes hard**: it fails for rule 86, rule 30's own mirror, at a third
76	  of the cells tested. This project has twice been caught by a check that was
77	  symmetric, and an orientation-sensitive claim is the opposite of that.
78	  Rule 150's centre column is constantly black so it has no maximal run at
79	  all and the claim is vacuous there — and the reasoning genuinely does not
80	  transfer: for `l XOR c XOR r` the sideways inverse gives
81	  `cell(t,−1) = cell(t,1)` under a black centre, not `cell(t,−1) = 0`.
82	  `C3` **fails the filter in the way that matters**: its *reasoning* is
83	  OR-specific (the forbidden adjacent-black pair is simply false for 150 and
84	  90), but its *conclusion* holds for 150, 90, 110 and 60 as well — and, worse,
85	  for a fair coin, whose triangle density is `1/2 < 2/3`. So `C3` separates
86	  rule 30's picture from an all-black one and from nothing else. Recorded in
87	  its own entry below; I had written the opposite before running this.
88	- **Crystal 67, the ensemble filter.** Nothing here is measure-theoretic, and
89	  `centerColumn_trace_uniform` is the counting form of `C2`'s fence: every
90	  column word of length `n+1` has exactly `2^n` windows, so no count over
91	  windows distinguishes one column word from another.
92	- **Crystal 29** says of the row count that "only `b(t) ≥ 3` and `b(t) ≤ 2t+1`
93	  (the cone) are provable, and neither is worth a node". `C3` improves that —
94	  weakly, and only against the cone.
95	- **Crystals A3**, no bound below `1` on a left damage front, is what stops
96	  `C1`'s run bound being sharpened from `O(a)` toward the true `O(log a)`: the
97	  alternation a run forces enters the transient band at depth `≈ 0.25a`, and to
98	  profit from that one would have to know where the band is.
99	
100	**The three routes the topic named, each closed.**
101	
102	**(1) A sparse set of cut points that rule 30 supplies.** Dead on the
103	localisation lemma's own hypothesis, before any measurement.
104	`centerColumn_density_tendsto_half_of_nearby_cuts` asks that *for every* `d`
105	there be, past some `N₀`, a cut `M ≤ N` with `d·(N − M) ≤ N` — a cut inside
106	`[N(1 − 1/d), N]` for every `d` and all large `N`. A set with that property is
107	not sparse in any useful sense: it must meet **every multiplicative window**,
108	however narrow. Every rule-30-supplied set on the board is exponentially sparse
109	and admits `d = 1` and nothing more: worst relative gap `0.99996` for the period
110	doublings `3, 8, 29, 400, 87867, 2107985255`, `0.99994` for the eventually-white
111	left diagonals `2, 7, 28, 399, 53207, 58286, 87866, 1420878968`, `0.5` for the
112	powers of two (`explorer/talus7_analyse.mjs`). Granting admissibility would buy
113	nothing anyway: at those cuts the excess is the size it is at a general `N`
114	(`|E|/√N` at most `0.72`, `1.41`, `1.56` on the three sets against `1.41`,
115	`1.13`, `2.00` for a fair coin on the same sets, to `N = 10^7`). The lemma is a
116	real theorem and its content is *"you may skip the `N` between cuts"*; it is not
117	a licence to check a thin set.
118	
119	**(2) The forcing laws' coverage.** Dead twice, once by proof and once by
120	measurement, and the proof is the one to keep. `column_succ_of_black` and
121	`centre_forced_after_double_white` are theorems about an **arbitrary** `Config`.
122	By crystal 40 every Bool sequence `b` is the centre column of some configuration
123	white on `x ≥ 1`, so both laws hold with `b` in place of the centre column, for
124	every `b`. **A consequence of them alone is therefore true of every Bool
125	sequence and can bound nothing.** Concretely, the law `c(t+1) = ¬L(t)` is not a
126	constraint on `c` at all: it is `sideways_inverse` at the origin,
127	`L(t) = c(t+1) XOR (c(t) OR R(t))`, read backwards, so it *defines* column `−1`
128	from columns `0` and `1` rather than restricting column `0`. Measured on the
129	seed, "`c(t+1) = ¬L(t)` holds exactly when `c(t) OR col₁(t)`" fails **0 of
130	199,999** times — the identity confirming itself. And the coverage figure is a
131	coin's (`explorer/talus7_coverage.mjs`, `T = 200,000`):
132	
133	| boundary | `dens(c)` | `dens(col 1)` | `dens(c OR col 1)` | double-white trigger |
134	|---|---|---|---|---|
135	| the seed | 0.5004 | 0.5007 | **0.7508** | 0.1251 |
136	| coin `b`, seed `9e3779b9` | 0.4999 | 0.4994 | **0.7495** | 0.1251 |
137	| coin `b`, seed `12345` | 0.4995 | 0.5014 | **0.7504** | 0.1263 |
138	| coin `b`, seed `deadbeef` | 0.5014 | 0.4998 | **0.7523** | 0.1257 |
139	
140	The `0.5004` is the centre column's own density quoted back, and the `0.7508`
141	is `1 − ¼` for two density-half sequences that look independent. Nothing was
142	measured about rule 30. This is no criticism of the node —
143	`centre_forced_after_double_white` is a fine theorem and its docstring already
144	says the figure is a measurement over one prefix — but the coverage cannot be
145	an ingredient of a P2 bound, and neither can any successor of it.
146	
147	**(3) The run structure.** Dead in two independent ways. Measured, the
148	run-length distribution **is** the geometric one and no moment is anomalous: at
149	`N = 10^7`, white runs have mean `1.99878` and `E[L²] = 5.99340`, black runs
150	`2.00056` and `6.00242`, against the geometric null's `2` and `6`; the
151	observed/expected ratio at every length `1..12` sits in `[0.94, 1.03]`, which is
152	a fair coin's own scatter on the same run (`explorer/talus7_analyse.mjs`). The
153	longest runs below `10^7` are `22` white and `23` black — `log₂ N` behaviour,
154	and the topic's "block of 16 at `M = 22711`" is that same phenomenon seen
155	earlier and smaller. And, second, **even a perfect run bound cannot give P2**:
156	if every run below `N` had length at most `c·log N` there would be at least
157	`N/(c log N)` runs, so the minority colour would appear at least
158	`N/(2c log N)` times and `|E(N)| ≤ N(1 − 1/(c log N))`, which is not `o(N)`.
159	The run route is capped below the target however sharp it is made, so it is not
160	worth sharpening.
161	
162	**The excess itself, measured as far as this session could reach.** To
163	`N = 10^7` (`explorer/talus7_deep.mjs`, 28 minutes): `E(10^7) = 4440`, i.e.
164	`1.404 √N`; minimum `−257` at `172,711`; maximum `4605` at `9,985,347`; first
165	negative at `N = 127`; last non-positive at `N = 195,112`, so the excess is
166	strictly positive over the last 98% of the range, with only 170 sign changes.
167	Three of those look unlike a coin, so they were nulled against **40 fair-coin
168	draws of the same length** (`explorer/talus7_null.mjs`):
169	
170	| statistic | rule 30 | coin median | draws at least as extreme |
171	|---|---|---|---|
172	| sign changes | 170 | 1327 | **6 of 40** |
173	| `min E` | −257 | −2159 | **5 of 40** |
174	| last `N` with `E ≤ 0` | 195,112 | 9,903,690 | **2 of 40** |
175	
176	The three are the arcsine law seen from three sides and are strongly dependent,
177	so jointly this is `p ≈ 0.1`, not a finding. **Reported as a plain negative:
178	after `10^7` rows, nothing about the centre column's excess is outside a fair
179	coin's scatter.**
180	
181	**One route the topic did not name, and it is the only one with content.** The
182	**row** count. The rule's constraint is horizontal, so it bites on rows: two
183	adjacent black cells forbid a cell of the next row (crystal 8). The centre
184	column is one cell of each row, and `centerColumn_run_boundary` says exactly

329	### C3. A provable density bound for rows — and it does not separate rule 30 from a coin

332	every `t`,

## 1. The residual, in one paragraph

Time runs down the picture; the centre column is the vertical read at `x = 0`,
one cell per row. Prize 2 says the black cells of that column are half of it in
the limit, and the board has already turned that into a statement with no
division in it: with `count(N)` the black cells among the first `N`, the excess
`E(N) = 2·count(N) − N` must be `o(N)`
(`centerColumn_density_tendsto_half_iff_excess`). What is missing is not a
better reformulation. It is **one true sentence about `E(N)` that is false for
some Bool sequence** — anything that uses the automaton at all. Twelve P2 nodes
are proved and ten are counting identities that hold of any `ℕ → Bool`; the two
that name rule 30 name it trivially. So the residual is not "prove
`E(N) = o(N)`" so much as "say *anything* about `E(N)` that a coin could fail",
and the reason that is hard can be put in one line: **rule 30 is a law along a
row, and the centre column is transverse to every row.** The rule constrains
three horizontally adjacent cells; two adjacent black cells in a row forbid a
cell of the next row, and that is a real constraint with real consequences
(§3, `C3`, `C4`). Two vertically adjacent cells of the centre column forbid
nothing, and cannot, because by crystal 40 the centre column is a **free
coordinate**: for every Bool sequence `b` there is a configuration, white at
every `x ≥ 1` at time `0`, whose centre column is exactly `b`. The residual
therefore lives in the one place that is not free — the left cone, the leftmost
black cell, the same ingredient Jen's and Kopra's theorems need for P1 — and
the only thing the cone gives the centre column is a bound on its **runs**,
which is capped in principle at `|E(N)| ≤ N(1 − 1/(c·log N))` and cannot reach
`o(N)` however sharp it is made.

### C1. A run of the centre column is no longer than its own start time

**The claim.** In English: while the centre column stays black, the picture
immediately to its left is forced to be a checkerboard, one further cell for
each further step — and the cone will not allow a checkerboard, because the two
leftmost cells of every row are both black. So a black stretch cannot be longer
than the time at which it starts.

In the project's vocabulary, in two parts.

*The lemma (the forced alternation).* For all `a ≥ 1` and `L ≥ 1`, if
`evolve t 0 = true` for every `t ∈ [a, a + L)`, then

    evolve a (-(j : ℤ)) = decide (j % 2 = 0)   for every j < L.

*The bound.* Under the same hypothesis, `L ≤ a`. The same method gives

monotone there, so the run splits into a stretch forcing an all-white triangle

maximal run beginning at `a` ends by `2a`, so run starts at most double, so
there are at least `log₂N − O(1)` maximal runs below `N`, so each colour occurs
at least `(log₂N)/2 − O(1)` times and

    |E(N)| ≤ N − log₂ N + O(1).

That is false for a constant Bool sequence, so it does what the topic literally
asks. It is also worth `23` at `N = 10^7`, so it does nothing else, and by the

### C3. A provable density bound for rows — and it does not separate rule 30 from a coin

**The claim.** Write `b(t)` for the number of black cells in row `t`. Then for
every `t`,

    b(t+1) + 2·b(t) ≤ 4t + 5,

and consequently the black cells of the first `T` rows number at most
`(2/3)T² + T + 1/3` of the `T²` cells in the triangle: the triangle's black
density is at most `2/3 + O(1/T)`, where the cone alone gives `1`.

*Why.* Rule 30 is `l XOR (c OR r)`, so a black cell of row `t+1` at position `i`
requires `¬(cell(t, i−1) ∧ cell(t, i))` — crystal 8's forbidden block. Row `t`
has exactly `b(t) − ρ(t)` adjacent black pairs, with `ρ(t)` its number of
maximal black runs, so `b(t+1) ≤ (2t+3) − (b(t) − ρ(t))`. Runs are separated by
at least one white and both cone edges are black, so
`ρ(t) ≤ (2t+1−b(t)) + 1`. Substituting gives the inequality; summing over
`t < T` gives the density.

provable" with a bound of `2/3`, and it is the sharpest available statement of

between horizontally adjacent cells, so it bounds a row count and says nothing
whatever about a count down a column.** Towards P2, nothing — and **it does not
even do what the topic asked**, because a fair coin's triangle has density `1/2`
and satisfies the bound comfortably. It separates rule 30's picture from an
all-black one and from nothing else. The filter run in §2 makes that concrete:
rules 90, 110, 150 and 60 satisfy it too, for the different reason that their
pictures are sparse. What is rule-30-specific is the **derivation**, not the
statement.

### C4. The exact row identity, which does separate rule 30 from a coin

**The claim.** With `ρ(t)` the number of maximal black runs of row `t` and
`G₂(t)` the number of **interior** white gaps of length at least `2`,

    b(t+1) = ρ(t) + 2·G₂(t) + 2.

*Why.* `rule30_run_boundary` says a cell is black next step exactly at one of
three local patterns: the leftmost cell of a black run (`ρ` of them), the cell
just right of a run followed by two whites, and the cell just left of a run
preceded by two whites. Inside the cone the two outer gaps are infinite, which
is the `+2`; each interior gap of length `≥ 2` is counted once from each side.

**What it would give.** This is the one statement in the document that a fair
coin fails outright — a coin's rows are independent, so no identity ties

is not?** This session's one piece of content is that rule 30's local law

not for any measured anomaly.
